name: Levator Scapulae Stretch
summary: A targeted static stretch for the neck and upper back that lengthens the levator scapulae via cervical flexion, contralateral rotation, and lateral flexion.

setup: Sit upright on a chair or stand tall with neutral posture.
Anchor the shoulder of the side you wish to stretch by placing that hand behind your lower back or gripping the underside of your chair seat.
Rotate your head roughly 45 degrees away from the target side.
steps: Gently tilt your chin down toward your collarbone or armpit until you feel a mild stretch along the back and side of your neck.
Place your free hand lightly on the crown of your head to add gentle overpressure, without yanking or forcing the movement.
Hold the position for the desired duration while breathing slowly and evenly.
Gently release the hand pressure, return your head to neutral, and repeat on the opposite side.
instructions.breathing: Maintain slow, deep diaphragmatic breaths, relaxing further into the stretch with each exhalation.

common_faults.fault: Yanking aggressively on the head and neck
common_faults.correction: Use only the light weight of the hand to apply gentle overpressure.

common_faults.fault: Allowing the stretched shoulder to shrug upward
common_faults.correction: Actively anchor the arm downward by sitting on your hand or holding the chair seat to keep the scapula depressed.

precautions: Stop immediately if you experience sharp pain, dizziness, or radiating tingling into the arm.
